risk_if_not_implemented: Without Role-Based Physical Access, users, services and processes may obtain or retain access beyond authorized need, enabling misuse or escalation. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Excessive or Unauthorized Privilege (R-AC-2), Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Monitoring Physical Access
compensating_control_1.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to monitor for, detect and respond to physical security incidents.
compensating_control_1.justification: Monitoring Physical Access (PES-13) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Role-Based Physical Access (PES-07) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Access Enforcement
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Logical Access Control (LAC) permissions that conform to the principle of "least privilege."
compensating_control_2.justification: Access Enforcement (IAC-25) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Role-Based Physical Access (PES-07) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
